This file states the three data generating processes (DGPs) in workflow/scripts/lib/dgp.R as formal models. Each section names the function that implements it.

Notation

Symbol Argument Default Meaning
\(S\) n_sets number of independent data sets
\(n\) n_obs observations in one data set
\(n_{\max}\) n_obs_max rows drawn before the first \(n\) are kept
\(D\) n_dim = length(beta) 3 columns of \(X\), intercept included
\(\beta\) beta make_beta_coeff() coefficients
\(\Delta\) out_dev outlier deviation
\(n_{\text{out}}\) n_obs_out 1 number of outliers
\(\sigma^2\) sigma2_d 1 Gaussian noise variance

The data sets \(s = 1, \dots, S\) are independent. The formulas below are for one data set, so the index \(s\) is dropped.

The outlier set is the first \(n_{\text{out}}\) observations:

\[ \mathcal{O} = \{1, \dots, \min(n_{\text{out}}, n)\}. \]

Shared parts

Coefficients

make_beta_coeff(beta_t, n_dim = 3, beta_other = 1, beta_intercept = 0) returns

\[ \beta = (\beta_0, \beta_1, \dots, \beta_{D-2}, \beta_t) = (0, 1, \dots, 1, \beta_t). \]

Model A omits the last covariate. Model B includes it. So \(\beta_t\) is the effect that only model B can capture.

Covariates

For each observation \(i = 1, \dots, n\):

\[ x_i = (1, x_{i1}, \dots, x_{i,D-1}), \qquad x_{ij} \overset{\text{iid}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(0, 1). \]

All three families draw the covariates in the same way.

Common random numbers

Each function draws \(n_{\max}\) rows and keeps the first \(n\). Thus cells with a different \(n\) share the first \(n\) covariate rows. The Gaussian noise and the uniforms of the binomial and Poisson models are also drawn for \(n_{\max}\) rows. So cells also share the first \(n\) responses, up to the change in \(\eta_i\) that the outlier makes.

Gaussian model

Function: make_data_gaussian().

\[ \begin{aligned} y_i &= x_i^\top \beta + \varepsilon_i, \\ \varepsilon_i &\sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_i, \sigma^2), \\ \mu_i &= \begin{cases} \Delta \sqrt{\sigma^2 + \lVert \beta \rVert_2^2} & i \in \mathcal{O}, \\ 0 & \text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{aligned} \]

Equivalently, \(y_i \sim \mathcal{N}(x_i^\top \beta + \mu_i, \sigma^2)\).

  • The shift scales with the marginal standard deviation of \(y_i\): \(\operatorname{Var}(x_i^\top \beta) = \sum_{j \ge 1} \beta_j^2\).
  • The code uses sum(beta^2). This sum includes \(\beta_0^2\). With the default \(\beta_0 = 0\) the two are equal.

Binomial (Bernoulli) model

Function: make_data_binomial().

\[ \begin{aligned} \eta_i &= x_i^\top \beta, \\ \tilde\eta_i &= \begin{cases} \eta_i - \Delta \, s(\eta_i) & i \in \mathcal{O}, \\ \eta_i & \text{otherwise}, \end{cases} \\ y_i &\sim \operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left(\operatorname{logit}^{-1}(\tilde\eta_i)\right), \end{aligned} \]

with the sign function sign_pos():

\[ s(x) = \begin{cases} -1 & x < 0, \\ +1 & x \ge 0. \end{cases} \]

  • The shift moves \(\eta_i\) towards the other class. A large \(\Delta\) makes the outlier almost surely the class that its covariates argue against.
  • \(s(0) = +1\), so the shift is never zero.
  • The code draws \(u_i \sim \mathcal{U}(0, 1)\) and sets \(y_i = \mathbb{1}\{u_i < \operatorname{logit}^{-1}(\tilde\eta_i)\}\).
  • \(\Delta\) is on the logit scale.

Poisson model

Function: make_data_poisson(). Constants: POIS_SCALE \(= c = 0.5\) and POIS_INTERCEPT \(= b_0 = 1\).

The coefficients are rescaled. The intercept is replaced:

\[ b = (b_0, \, c\,\beta_1, \dots, c\,\beta_{D-1}). \]

\[ \begin{aligned} \eta_i &= x_i^\top b, \\ \tilde\eta_i &= \begin{cases} \eta_i + \Delta & i \in \mathcal{O}, \\ \eta_i & \text{otherwise}, \end{cases} \\ y_i &\sim \operatorname{Poisson}\!\left(\exp(\tilde\eta_i)\right). \end{aligned} \]

  • The shift is always upwards. A downward shift gives counts near 0. Such counts are common at a rate near \(e\), so the outlier would be weak.
  • \(\Delta\) is on the log scale. The outlier rate is \(e^{\Delta}\) times the rate of its covariates.
  • The code draws \(u_i \sim \mathcal{U}(0, 1)\) and sets \(y_i = F^{-1}(u_i \mid \exp(\tilde\eta_i))\), with \(F\) the Poisson distribution function (qpois()).
  • With the defaults, the median of \(\eta_i\) is 1, so the median rate is \(e\). beta_intercept has no effect.

Summary

Gaussian Binomial Poisson
Linear predictor \(x_i^\top \beta\) \(x_i^\top \beta\) \(x_i^\top b\), \(b = (1, 0.5\,\beta_{1:})\)
Link identity logit log
Outlier shift \(+\Delta \sqrt{\sigma^2 + \lVert\beta\rVert^2}\) on \(\varepsilon_i\) \(-\Delta\, s(\eta_i)\) on \(\eta_i\) \(+\Delta\) on \(\eta_i\)
Scale of \(\Delta\) SD of \(y\) logit log

One draw for each family

set.seed(1)
beta <- make_beta_coeff(1)
n <- 100

op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
for (fam in c("gaussian", "binomial", "poisson")) {
  d <- make_data_family(fam, 1, n, n, beta, out_dev = 5)
  eta <- drop(d$X[, , 1] %*% beta)
  plot(eta, d$y[, 1], col = c(2, rep(1, n - 1)), pch = 19, cex = 0.6,
       xlab = expression(x^T * beta), ylab = "y", main = fam)
}

par(op)

The red point is the outlier (\(i = 1\)).

Rule data on example cells

This section runs workflow/scripts/generate_data.R, the script of rule data, outside Snakemake. A mock snakemake object gives the script its input. The input comes from config/small.yaml and config/cells_small.tsv.

Input

config <- yaml::read_yaml("config/small.yaml")
cells <- read.delim(config$cells, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
# As read_cells() and N_OBS_MAX in workflow/rules/common.smk.
n_obs_max <- max(cells$n_obs)
example <- c(gaussian = "n64_b1_o20",
             binomial = "bin_n64_b1_o5",
             poisson = "pois_n64_b1_o2")
cells[match(example, cells$cell), ]
##              cell   family n_obs beta_t out_dev n_chunks
## 8      n64_b1_o20 gaussian    64      1      20        2
## 16  bin_n64_b1_o5 binomial    64      1       5        1
## 24 pois_n64_b1_o2  poisson    64      1       2        2
config[c("n_sets_train", "n_sets_test_gaussian", "n_sets_test_binomial",
         "n_sets_test_poisson", "seed")]
## $n_sets_train
## [1] 100
## 
## $n_sets_test_gaussian
## [1] 200
## 
## $n_sets_test_binomial
## [1] 50
## 
## $n_sets_test_poisson
## [1] 20
## 
## $seed
## [1] 2958319
n_obs_max
## [1] 64

Run the script

setClass("MockSnakemake", representation(
  params = "list", output = "list", log = "list", source = "function"
))

run_rule_data <- function(cell_name) {
  row <- cells[cells$cell == cell_name, ]
  cell <- list(family = row$family, n_obs = row$n_obs,
               beta_t = row$beta_t, out_dev = row$out_dev,
               n_chunks = row$n_chunks)
  dir <- file.path(tempdir(), cell_name)
  dir.create(dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  snakemake <- new("MockSnakemake",
    params = list(cell = cell, n_sets_train = config$n_sets_train,
                  n_sets_test_gaussian = config$n_sets_test_gaussian,
                  n_sets_test_binomial = config$n_sets_test_binomial,
                  n_sets_test_poisson = config$n_sets_test_poisson,
                  n_obs_max = n_obs_max, seed = config$seed),
    output = list(train = file.path(dir, "train.rds"),
                  test = file.path(dir, "test.rds"),
                  info = file.path(dir, "data_info.rds")),
    log = list(file.path(dir, "data.log")),
    source = function(f) source(file.path("workflow/scripts", f))
  )
  env <- new.env()
  env$snakemake <- snakemake
  open_before <- getAllConnections()
  source("workflow/scripts/generate_data.R", local = env)
  # Undo start_log(): restore the message stream and close the log file.
  sink(type = "message")
  for (con in setdiff(getAllConnections(), open_before)) {
    close(getConnection(con))
  }
  list(cell = cell,
       train = readRDS(snakemake@output$train),
       test = readRDS(snakemake@output$test),
       info = readRDS(snakemake@output$info))
}

out <- lapply(example, run_rule_data)

Output

The script writes three files for each cell:

  • train.rds: X as [n_obs, n_dim, n_sets_train], y as [n_obs, n_sets_train].
  • test.rds: the pooled test sets. X as [n_obs * n_sets_test_<family>, n_dim], y as a vector.
  • data_info.rds: y_test_var, the variance of the test y.
for (fam in names(out)) {
  o <- out[[fam]]
  cat(sprintf(
    "%-8s train X %s, y %s | test X %s, y %d | y_test_var %.3f\n",
    fam, paste(dim(o$train$X), collapse = " x "),
    paste(dim(o$train$y), collapse = " x "),
    paste(dim(o$test$X), collapse = " x "), length(o$test$y),
    o$info$y_test_var))
}
## gaussian train X 64 x 3 x 100, y 64 x 100 | test X 12800 x 3, y 12800 | y_test_var 21.655
## binomial train X 64 x 3 x 100, y 64 x 100 | test X 3200 x 3, y 3200 | y_test_var 0.250
## poisson  train X 64 x 3 x 100, y 64 x 100 | test X 1280 x 3, y 1280 | y_test_var 32.226

Checks

The outliers in the test data are the rows \((s - 1)\,n + 1\). The table compares the outliers with the other observations. It also compares the mean of \(y\) with its expected value under the formal model.

For the binomial family, the mean of \(y\) does not show the outlier. So for this family \(y\) is replaced by the indicator that \(y_i\) is the class against the sign of \(\eta_i\), \(\mathbb{1}\{y_i \ne \mathbb{1}\{\eta_i \ge 0\}\}\).

# Linear predictor of the formal model, before the outlier shift.
true_eta <- function(family, X, beta) {
  if (family == "poisson") {
    beta <- beta * POIS_SCALE
    beta[1] <- POIS_INTERCEPT
  }
  drop(X %*% beta)
}

# Expected y of each observation under the formal model.
expected_y <- function(family, eta, out_dev, is_out, beta) {
  switch(family,
    gaussian = eta + is_out * out_dev * sqrt(1 + sum(beta^2)),
    binomial = plogis(eta - is_out * out_dev * sign_pos(eta)),
    poisson = exp(eta + is_out * out_dev)
  )
}

checks <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(out), function(fam) {
  o <- out[[fam]]
  beta <- make_beta_coeff(o$cell$beta_t)
  n <- o$cell$n_obs
  is_out <- (seq_along(o$test$y) - 1) %% n == 0
  eta <- true_eta(fam, o$test$X, beta)
  ey <- expected_y(fam, eta, o$cell$out_dev, is_out, beta)
  y <- o$test$y
  if (fam == "binomial") {
    y <- ifelse(eta >= 0, 1 - y, y)
    ey <- ifelse(eta >= 0, 1 - ey, ey)
  }
  data.frame(
    family = fam,
    outlier_share = mean(is_out),
    mean_y_out = mean(y[is_out]),
    expected_out = mean(ey[is_out]),
    mean_y_other = mean(y[!is_out]),
    expected_other = mean(ey[!is_out]),
    y_test_var = o$info$y_test_var,
    var_check = mean((o$test$y - mean(o$test$y))^2)
  )
}))
knitr::kable(checks, digits = 3)
family outlier_share mean_y_out expected_out mean_y_other expected_other y_test_var var_check
gaussian 0.016 34.824 34.741 -0.009 -0.009 21.655 21.655
binomial 0.016 0.960 0.968 0.283 0.275 0.250 0.250
poisson 0.016 28.300 27.663 3.693 3.540 32.226 32.226

Plots

Each column is one family. The top row shows the first training set. The bottom row shows the pooled test sets. Red points are outliers. The x-axis is the linear predictor \(\eta_i\) of the formal model, before the outlier shift. The binomial \(y\) is jittered.

# One x-range for each family, shared by its train and test plots.
xlims <- lapply(out, function(o) {
  beta <- make_beta_coeff(o$cell$beta_t)
  range(true_eta(o$cell$family, o$train$X[, , 1], beta),
        true_eta(o$cell$family, o$test$X, beta))
})

op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
for (part in c("train", "test")) {
  for (fam in names(out)) {
    o <- out[[fam]]
    beta <- make_beta_coeff(o$cell$beta_t)
    if (part == "train") {
      X <- o$train$X[, , 1]
      y <- o$train$y[, 1]
    } else {
      X <- o$test$X
      y <- o$test$y
    }
    is_out <- (seq_along(y) - 1) %% o$cell$n_obs == 0
    if (fam == "binomial") y <- jitter(y, amount = 0.08)
    plot(true_eta(fam, X, beta), y, pch = 19, xlim = xlims[[fam]],
         cex = if (part == "train") 0.6 else 0.3,
         col = ifelse(is_out, "red", adjustcolor("black", 0.3)),
         xlab = expression(eta), ylab = "y",
         main = sprintf("%s, %s (%s)", fam, part,
                        if (part == "train") "set 1"
                        else paste(length(y), "points")))
  }
}

par(op)
